answers.answer: Each office card rolls one die plus one per fatigue; Chairman adds one. Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire. Move the member to Pensioners, flip the card to Vacant Offices, and return its fatigue to supply.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → London Season: “Add one per fatigue on that card; Chairman also adds one”; “5+: retire”; “Move retiree to Pensioners, flip card into Vacant Offices, return its fatigue to supply.”

answers.answer: Only players who retired at least one pensioner select or discard one display card, in descending actual total retirement spending. Ties go to most total windows including new prizes, then clockwise from PM. No replacements occur during selection; if display empties, skip remaining eligible players. Then discard all remaining cards and refill exactly three (prestige faceup, blackmail facedown). Return remaining Pensioners to supplies.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → London Season: “Players who retired at least one pensioner”; “descending actual total retirement spending”; ties “most total windows…then clockwise from PM”; display and pensioner cleanup.

answers.answer: At phase start check whether the marker already matches the chosen main action; if so, that action may be taken twice. Move the marker onto the chosen action afterward. Only the latest passed extra-action law can grant an extra action; it is never doubled and does not move the marker. With four vacant offices and a doubled Writer action, place three writers total (the vacancy bonus applies once).
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Family: steps 1–4; Enlist Writer: “With at least four vacant offices, place one additional writer once this turn, so a doubled Writer action can place three total.”

answers.answer: After family actions, while Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one, repeating. If Debt is zero, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible preserving order. The initial purchase fee is paid to the bank; no share-seeking cash goes to Company treasuries.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Family: “New Company shares”; Seek Share: pay bank; “never pays family cash into Company treasuries.”

answers.answer: Fill vacancies in ascending card-back number. Hiring own family for an ordinary office requires verbal consent from every other player represented in that office’s candidate pool. On promotion, fatigue transfers to the new card and the old card joins hiring order as vacant. With no candidate or a vacant hirer, skip it; it remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.
answers.evidence: Hiring: opening paragraph and Nepotism table: ascending order, pool consent, fatigue transfer, and skip condition.

answers.answer: Former Chairman announces the number of shares needed for a pure majority (more than half current shares). Any shareholder may campaign; the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. If none does, former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including self. The winner’s Company share moves into Chairman slot and remains a share for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in firms.
answers.evidence: Hiring → Chairman election: majority, campaign, fallback; “It still counts as a share… but cannot be traded or invested in firms.”

answers.answer: An office check commits cash from that office’s treasury and pays it to the bank. Gather dice, subtract penalties, roll and use the lowest die: 1–2 success; 3–4 failure, retry if resources and office limits allow; 5–6 catastrophe, ending that office’s actions, returning officeholder to supply, discarding fatigue and flipping its card to Vacant Offices. Do not take an action with no effect or chance of success.
answers.evidence: Company Operation → Success checks: treasury payment, roll outcomes, catastrophe destinations, and dead-action rule.

answers.answer: Chairman may borrow up to three Debt freely, adding £5 Balance each. Each further advance needs consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares (Chairman counts); never advance beyond the Debt track end. Chairman must allocate all Balance to other offices’ treasuries, reducing Balance for each transfer; borrowing and allocation may be interleaved. Existing office cash stays there.
answers.evidence: Actions → Chairman: voluntary borrowing, consent threshold, track limit, and allocation duties.

answers.answer: Shipping must spend until £2 or less remains. It can lease an extra ship for £2; fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without owner consent; or buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Acquired ships go to any sea zone, including China once created; extra ships last until Refresh.
answers.evidence: Actions → Manager of Shipping: full budget, costs, destinations and prerequisite.

answers.answer: Declare home region and reachable regions connected by open orders, subject to available ship capacity. Pay £1 per die from President’s treasury and subtract one die per declared nonhome region. Failure may be retried if affordable; catastrophe removes President; each President can succeed at most once per turn. A successful Trade fills up to one order per ship in that Presidency’s sea zone: first writer in home port; each later order extends this Trade’s own connected route. Writers from other Presidencies do not extend it; writers do not limit capacity, so filled tokens cover remaining ships. Cannot fill another President’s home region. Balance receives printed order value, or half rounded down if a firm filled it this turn; President gets £1/order and writer owners £1/writer.
answers.evidence: Actions → Presidency operations and Trade: declare/check constraints, capacity/routes, protected home regions and payouts.

answers.answer: Deploy may target own Presidency’s home, any associated region, or a region bordering an associated region, but not another home or another Presidency’s Company-controlled region. A Company region must have unrest or a closed order. Exhaust officers/regiments for one die each and local alliances for printed dice; subtract target plus all other regions in its empire (target counted once; Company defense is zero). After every attempt, roll one die per officer exhausted; each 6 removes that officer, whether check succeeded or failed.
answers.evidence: Actions → Commanders and Deploy: steps 1–3, target, dice/penalty and post-attempt officer loss.

answers.answer: On successful Deploy, loot is £4 per target tower plus faceup loot modifier, minimum surviving participating officers plus one for Commander. Distribute repeated payout cycles: Commander first (£1 for Commander and each used surviving officer of theirs), other families clockwise (£1 per used surviving officer), then bank (£1 per used regiment and alliance piece); repeat until loot gone. Commander gets one trophy per target tower. Successful control removes tower/dome, opens orders, removes unrest and creates Governorship/control markers unless already Company-controlled or Governor General applies. Catastrophe returns half Commander-family trophies rounded up and Commander member to supply; exhausted officers still check losses.
answers.evidence: Actions → Commanders and Deploy: success loot/payout/control and catastrophe paragraphs.

answers.answer: Governor uses its printed dice pool; each attempt rolls current pool without penalty, then reduces it by one regardless of result. Success gives £1, or £2 if immediately preceding roll was unsuccessful, then exactly one option: build one ship stage, commission one regiment into associated Presidency’s Army, or tax £2 unsplit into Company Balance or that Presidency treasury. Any failure adds one unrest; catastrophe also removes holder. Each tax after the first this turn adds unrest. Repeat until stopping, no dice, or catastrophe. The text does not explicitly say whether prior failed roll sets the £2 bonus across an intervening successful roll; “immediately preceding roll” suggests only the last roll matters.
answers.evidence: Actions → Governors: Administer tables and repeat/stop sentence; quote “£2 if the immediately preceding roll was unsuccessful.”

answers.answer: If expenses exceed Balance, take £5 emergency loans, advancing Debt one each until track end; continue taking loans even at max Debt. New emergency Debt adds no current-turn expense. After loans, set Balance to zero. One or two loans lower Standing one; three or more lower it two. Then compare remaining Balance with expectations at current Standing and lower Standing one if short. Chairman may then pay affordable dividends; if total paid is strictly greater than expectations, Standing rises one.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Revenue: Expenses, Expectations and Dividends.

answers.answer: For a Company-targeted Crisis, resolve primary attack first, then secondary rebellions in Bombay→Madras→Bengal order; within each Presidency its Commander chooses associated-region order. Primary normal Crisis strength is normal attack strength plus target unrest; secondary Rebellion strength is only unrest there. For Company defense, associated Commander exhausts active Army pieces totaling strength (as much as possible), using alliance printed strength; alliances cannot split. If newly exhausted pieces match attack strength, defense succeeds: remove all target unrest and give Commander a trophy; if successful defense stops a normal primary Invasion, remove one attacker tower if possible. An indivisible alliance excess case is expressly unresolved. Vacant Commander is covered by Military Affairs, or Chairman if Military Affairs vacant; actor gains/loses no trophies.
answers.evidence: Events → Attacks on Company and Region Loss: order, strengths, defense test and unresolved alliance case.

answers.answer: Law support −1 or less fails: discard law, resolve dilemma’s failure text, Opposition Leader returns token and takes PM dial; new PM shifts proposed policy one adjacent space and resolves it. Support zero or more passes: place law among passed laws, PM takes passed-law token, resolve policy first then immediate law effects. Restore rotated voting cards after either outcome. If law causes Company failure, finish vote first.
answers.evidence: Parliament Meets → Resolution: failure/pass thresholds and sequence.

answers.answer: In 1758 and Long 1710, at turn start before London Season, PM may call special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt on lined spaces; must call if either is on starred space. Ordinary voting/threshold applies except there is no policy; PM may vote against; failure neither removes PM nor discards Deregulation law. Passing lowers Debt one per two current Debt, sets Standing to S, gives PM passed-law token and activates firms. Failure increases Company share scoring value by flipping/placing Court VP token (maximum ±3). 1813 starts deregulated; 1710 has no procedures in its scenario row.
answers.evidence: Deregulation: timing, lined/starred trigger, pass/fail outcomes and exceptions; Setup scenario table.

answers.answer: To form a firm, a player currently managing none returns an eligible Company share to supply or flips a workshop to invested side, flips their family board to firm charter, places a member as first firm share, sets value to leftmost and takes £5 from bank into London treasury. Investing with manager consent uses share/workshop contribution for a firm share plus £5 from bank to London. Firm share cap is ten; excess investment still adds £5 but no share. Cannot use Chairman share; cannot use any Company shares while Standing and/or Debt is lined; cannot use shares created this turn even after trading them. Invested workshops never revert and lose bonus/failure VP.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → Firms phase: investments: formation/investment rules.

answers.answer: Each firm gets exactly one trade attempt per turn. Managers secretly choose trade zone/home port and bid London cash, or Hobnob (no bid/trade/dividends). At associated Presidency beginning, reveal matching strategy and roll one die per £ bid, paying bid to bank; any 1/2 permits trade. Initiative equals ships minus successful bid dice (1s/2s); successful President Trade has same calculation using Presidency ships. Fill lowest initiative first, ties chosen by President, or if President vacant/never succeeds, after Commander/Governors with Chairman choosing ties. Firm fills up to ships+1 orders, starting home port and tracing its own route; each order once. Previously filled orders can be refilled for half listed revenue rounded down. Advance Value one space per full £6 added to India treasury.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → Firm strategies and competing trade: all paragraphs.

answers.answer: Firm expenses at Revenue start are £1 per charter ship plus higher of share count or Value, payable from either/both treasuries. Unable-to-pay firm dissolves unless rescued. Dissolution sends shares to Debtor’s Prison at −1 VP each, ships to matching shipyards, charter to family side; invested workshops remain invested. After expenses, manager may dividend from India only: each dividend pays £1 per share plus £1 manager; waiving requires shareholder choice and manager consent. Record total actual payout on Balance track; active non-Hobnob paying none records zero, Hobnob retains prior marker. Sweep remaining India money to London.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → Firm expenses, rescue and dividends.

answers.answer: Unlimited: Company Balance, VP and Vote tracks. Cash, trophy/passed-law tokens, dice and regiments may use proxies; other component supplies are limited and complete as much as possible when exhausted. All information public except facedown blackmail and temporarily concealed firm strategies/bids during selection.
answers.evidence: Components → Limits: exact unlimited and hidden-information statements.

answers.answer: Prestige enterprises retain type, power and policy effects and may be traded; shares may be traded (firm shares like Company shares). Used blackmail is faceup and cannot be traded; unused blackmail may be traded. Transfer of a share is represented by moving the family member to the new owner's area. The summary does not state every other negotiable/nonnegotiable item or a full negotiation inventory.
answers.evidence: Overview/Components; London Season: blackmail trading; Special Rules & Edge Cases → Negotiation: “Move the family member to new owner's area” (see section).

answers.answer: Immediate transfers are binding; promises of future behavior are not, except printed promise cards can be called to force their guaranteed effect if possible. Promise cards can be traded to a third party or back to guarantor. If multiple promises called together cannot all be fulfilled, guarantor chooses which to fulfill. Read each card’s timing and limits. Transferred resources cannot activate twice (example: a workshop paid this Bonuses phase does not pay again if sold during it). No promises may be called during Final Scoring.
answers.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases → Negotiation: “Immediate transfers are binding; promises of future behavior are not”; simultaneous calls; transferred-resource restriction; “No calling promises during Final Scoring.”

answers.answer: Use the scenario’s setup cards and add three extra cards for five players or six for six players, shuffle and deal evenly. Each takes listed cash, enterprises and positions; distribute listed holdings using table (office member plus matching card to owner; shares to Court; shipyard ship to listed zone or on yard unfitted). Each starting luxury gives 2 VP. Shuffle prestige and blackmail together, deal three display cards (prestige faceup, blackmail facedown), shuffle remaining laws.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3–4 and listed setup holding table.

answers.answer: End after scenario final turn or when Standing reaches failure. Normally failure is immediate; if during Events, finish that phase; legislation-caused failure finishes the vote before Final Scoring. Once game over, stop negotiations, promise calls and blackmail unless card explicitly permits final-scoring use. No negotiations or promise calls during any of Final Scoring.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: ending and Final Scoring restrictions.

answers.answer: Final Power totals enterprise/share power from current Power track (bottom two positions zero), +1 per passed-law token and trophy, +2 PM, plus printed card power including blackmail and applicable spouse. Awards: turns 1–3 most/second 3/1; turns 4–6 5/2; turns 7–8 8/4. Tied first each gets only lower award and no other award; tied second get none. Overall VP ties break by most windows, then clockwise from PM.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: Power award and winner tiebreak.

answers.answer: If Company survives, each Company share gains current Court VP value; if Company fails, each loses that value and each uninvested workshop gains 1 VP. Firm-share scoring and eligible special retirement happen before either branch whether Company survives or fails; firm retirements are not replaced by failure card. Then surviving Company triggers final office attrition/retirements; failure draws a Company failure card.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: Court/workshops, survival/failure and special retirement.

answers.answer: Spouses usually add VP, impose permanent restrictions and cannot be transferred. Required enterprise/share trades happen immediately on taking spouse. Retirement discounts stack, are personal, and each can be used once per London Season and once during Final Scoring.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → London Season: spouse and discount paragraphs.

answers.answer: If shipyard returns due to Violet Effingham or unpaid tax, its fitted ship stays in play. That yard cannot be purchased while matching ship remains in play; it becomes available after ship returns.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → London Season: Returned shipyard rule; Parliament policy table also covers tax.

answers.answer: Enlist Writer/Officer: no cash cost stated; place respectively in any Presidency Writers box or Officers-in-Training (writer may gain one additional once if ≥4 vacancies). Purchase Luxury: £4, +2 VP while owned and window icon (social). Purchase Shipyard: £2, take yard and matching ship unfitted on it, shipping enterprise with one vote and £1 bonus while fitted. Purchase Workshop: £5, manufacturing enterprise, two votes, £1 bonus; worth 1 VP on Company failure if uninvested. Seek Share: pay an empty queue space’s £2/£3/£3/£4/£5 price and put member there as applicant, not yet share.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Family action table.

answers.answer: If needing to place a family piece with none in supply, take one from any of your prizes and lose that prize’s printed VP; this also applies to firm-share creation. If no Family action is possible, take none and return opportunity marker to supply.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Family immediately before action table and final sentence of Family section.

answers.answer: If Court is empty, former Chairman automatically returns, placing a member from supply or, if needed and possible, from a prize (lose prize VP). If impossible, there is no Chairman. This is within Chairman election/hiring.
answers.evidence: Hiring → Chairman election: empty-Court fallback.

answers.answer: Chairman chooses Director from current officeholders except Chairman/Governor; if all offices vacant, any writer. Chairman chooses any writer as Shipping Manager. Chairman chooses Military Affairs from Presidential Commander, else any officer, else any trainee. Director chooses President from associated Presidency writer or Governor. Associated President chooses Governor from region writer/officer, not Commander. Chairman chooses China Superintendent from any writer, hired immediately on creation. Governor General replaces Director and is hired same way. Hirer vacancy causes skip; a skipped office remains vacant.
answers.evidence: Hiring table and opening Hiring paragraph.

answers.answer: Special Envoy checks can repeat; each costs £1 treasury per die, no penalty. Success either opens one closed order in a non-Company region, or opens China by placing overlay/card and having Chairman immediately hire a writer. After all envoys, Director may transfer up to two pieces (one writer or ship each) between any Presidencies/sea zones, including China once created. Cannot transfer while still taking envoys.
answers.evidence: Actions → Director of Trade.

answers.answer: Military Affairs first may transfer up to two officers/regiments between Armies, remaining in top half; next assigns every trainee to any Army top half; finally appoints Commanders. If vacant or another family has more total pieces in Army than current Commander’s family, choose among families with most pieces; chosen officer becomes Commander and incumbent returns to top as officer. Tie with incumbent’s family does not replace them. Nepotism does not apply.
answers.evidence: Actions → Military Affairs.

answers.answer: Each President orders its Commander, Governors and own Trade, giving each position an opportunity; Commander/Governors may decline. Each position completes all actions before next, and Trade cannot interrupt. If President vacant, Chairman sets order only and cannot trade or approve local alliance purchase.
answers.evidence: Actions → Presidency operations and Trade.

answers.answer: Trade ships never exhaust; fitted player ships retain fatigue through Refresh. On nonfinal Refresh, writers on orders return to their associated Presidency’s Writers box, using dividers; filled tokens and dividers return to supply. Final turn skips Refresh.
answers.evidence: Actions → Trade capacity; Upkeep and Refresh table and final-turn rule.

answers.answer: Commander requests Presidency treasury money for printed-price local alliances; President must approve. Purchased alliances move to active/top half. Used for Deploy or defense, the whole alliance exhausts; strength cannot be split or reused that turn. Refresh also exhausts unused active alliances; alliances do not reactivate. Summary does not specify whether/how alliance purchase is mandatory relative to other action steps beyond this.
answers.evidence: Actions → Commanders and Deploy: alliance purchase and whole-piece exhaust; Upkeep and Refresh: active alliances exhaust.

answers.answer: In own Company region, Company defense strength/penalty is zero. If deploying just to reopen orders or clear unrest, there is no tower and thus zero tower trophies. With no tower or faceup loot modifier, minimum loot is surviving participating officers plus £1 for Commander, distributed normally.
answers.evidence: Actions → Commanders and Deploy: target clause, Company control procedure, and already Company-controlled region paragraph.

answers.answer: Building a Company ship requires two successful Build choices: first success places partial ship in Governor’s region; a later successful Build completes it into sea zone associated with that Governor’s President. Governor’s commissioned regiment goes to Army associated with that President; it has officer-like strength, pays loot to bank and has no officer-loss roll.
answers.evidence: Actions → Governors: Administer table.

answers.answer: China is created by successful Special Envoy or Envoy to China law; Chairman immediately hires a writer. Its treasury holds ships, not cash. Shipping/Director may send ships there. It acts after Bengal; China ships count Eastern for expenses, events, storms and laws.
answers.evidence: Actions → Superintendent of Trade in China; Director action; office order in Company Operation.

answers.answer: China gets one Trade attempt, one die per ship, only if Company regions have at least one export icon. The summary does not state whether an unsuccessful China check can be retried or whether no-export condition means no attempt; it says attempt only if icons exist. On success, count icons only in Company regions: Company Balance gets £4 per icon, Superintendent family gets £1 per icon from bank. It does not pay exports for non-Company icons.
answers.evidence: Actions → Superintendent of Trade in China: attempt condition and payout table.

answers.answer: When Governor General law passes, Governors become pensioners; remove their overlays and partial ships; return Governor/Director cards to box. Replace Director with Governor General, preserving holder and fatigue and ribbon position; no further Governors/overlays on conquest, and region losses skip Governor Elimination. The summary does not explain how subsequent conquests/region losses otherwise differ beyond these changes and printed Company symbols indicating controlled regions.
answers.evidence: Actions → Governor General: law effect and region loss rule.

answers.answer: Before Govern checks, add £3 Balance per Company region. Each Govern attempt costs £1 per die from its treasury, no penalty. Every rolled 6 adds one unrest to each Company region, even on success; failure adds another unrest to every Company region. Success gives £1 per Company region and requires choosing one benefit per region: complete Company ship into any zone including China; regiment in any Army; or £2 to Balance/any office treasury except own, with unrest in a Company region. Multiple tax choices this turn must put unrest in different regions. At most one successful Govern per turn.
answers.evidence: Actions → Governor General.

answers.answer: For each player-owned ship in storm zone, roll once: 1–2 nothing; 3–4 fatigue if unfatigued, sink if already fatigued; 5–6 sink. Sunk ship returns to yard unfatigued. Company and extra ships are exempt. China ships count Eastern. Firm ships face storms in strategy zone; Hobnob ships are exempt.
answers.evidence: Events in India → Storms; Deregulation → firm dividends paragraph.

answers.answer: When order newly closes, return any writer there to owner’s supply; flip filled token to closed. If event closes order in an already fully closed region, Cascade closes all open orders directly connected to region’s orders. If a connected order is already closed, instead close that region’s northernmost open order. If none open, it also Cascades. A region can initiate Cascade once per event tile but receive multiple Cascades’ effects.
answers.evidence: Events in India → Closing orders and Cascades.

answers.answer: Turmoil closes northernmost open order in top-stack region; if all closed, Cascade. Windfall pays owners £1 per writer in top-stack region and every bordering region. Shuffle: Elephant March, shuffle tile with remaining draw stack, then separately shuffle discards and place on top; if draw stack empty, March last instead.
answers.evidence: Events in India event table.

answers.answer: Leader: top-stack sovereign region gains one tower. If dominated, instead it rebels with printed explosion modifier. March only when Elephant was fully inside a Company region that successfully rebelled.
answers.evidence: Events in India event table → Leader.

answers.answer: Peace on a border opens orders connected across Elephant’s border and adds one tower to each touched non-Company region. Elephant fully in a region: instead open all its orders and remove its unrest. Then March in either case.
answers.evidence: Events in India event table → Peace.

answers.answer: For non-Company Invasion Crisis, attacker’s whole empire strength plus modifier must be strictly greater than defender’s whole empire strength; equal does not win. Success replaces defender flag with attacker dominated flag; taking capital shatters whole defender empire. If attacker has no empire, use free capital/star and matching small flag; if none available, no new empire/flags form. Failure removes one attacker tower.
answers.evidence: Events in India → Invasion Crisis.

answers.answer: For non-Company Rebellion, compare only rebelling region strength plus modifier to its sovereign capital strength; other empire regions excluded. Must be strictly greater, so tie fails. Success makes actor sovereign, removes its flag and closes orders (Cascade if already closed). Failure removes one tower from capital.
answers.evidence: Events in India → Rebellion Crisis.

answers.answer: On Region Loss, return half Commander’s family trophies rounded up and Commander to supply; roll once per officer in associated Army and each 6 removes officer. Eliminate Governor (card to unused, fatigue/member to supply), remove overlay, partial ship, unrest. Restore dome with one tower (or Foreign Invasion specified strength) and appropriate invasion flag; return control token loot-side down, region-symbol side up. Future conquest no loot modifier; region loses Presidency association. Invasion closes orders/Cascade; Rebellion/Foreign Invasion already close them. Standing loss escalates by losses this turn: first −1, second additional −2, etc. No other Company region is lost automatically.
answers.evidence: Events in India → Region Loss.

answers.answer: After successful Invasion Crisis, Elephant moves to successful capital (Imperial Ambitions); after other Marches it goes to top-stack region. Company region: fully inside. Dominated region: points toward sovereign. Sovereign: points across tile’s shape-marked border; if neighbor already dominated by actor, choose first clockwise neighbor not so dominated. If all neighbors dominated, use redirect-arrow shape’s border toward empire capital.
answers.evidence: Events in India → Elephant’s March.

answers.answer: Roll storm die for targets: West means Bombay, South Madras, East Bengal; all storms targets each; none means top-stack region. For each target roll ordinary die as attack strength. On success close all target orders (Cascade if already all closed), remove target flag and matching flags if capital, restore dome if Company-controlled, set towers to half die rounded down. March with circle shape only if Elephant was fully inside an invaded Company region. Foreign Invasion’s primary attack does not add unrest; unrest neither sets attack nor resulting tower strength. It still uses Company defense procedure and secondary unrest attacks.
answers.evidence: Events in India → Foreign Invasion; FAQ & Rulings → Foreign Invasion and unrest.

answers.answer: PM must draw at least one law, revealing one at a time. After one or two ordinary laws, may stop or continue up to three total; select any revealed law and discard others. Drawing a dilemma forces it to be selected and ends drawing. Before voting, move dial clockwise or counterclockwise to first policy matching chosen law’s bottom icon; this fixes target and consequence.
answers.evidence: Parliament Meets: law selection and policy paragraphs.

answers.answer: Tax policy: family pays bank £1 per owned target; unpaid target returns to supply, Chairman included; ship remains if shipyard returned and yard unavailable until ship returns. Window tax additionally charges windows on enterprises and each prize member; unpaid returns enterprise/prize member. Bonus: bank pays each family £1 per target owned. Power swaps target marker with next higher marker; if already highest, swap any other pair.
answers.evidence: Parliament Meets → Policy table.

answers.answer: Players vote starting with PM clockwise; each £1 family cash buys one vote plus printed card votes. Card votes usable only once across all rounds in the entire vote; rotate when used until resolution. PM may call another full round or stop after each; a no-vote round ends voting. Track support unlimited. Summary doesn’t expressly state a general stopping threshold beyond PM choice/no-vote round.
answers.evidence: Parliament Meets → Voting.

answers.answer: A supporter may later oppose, but once opposed cannot later support in that vote. Opposition Leader is biggest opponent; tied current holder retains role. With recipient consent, votes can be cast for someone already opposed or committing to oppose, added to their opposition total. PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprises opposing except forced “Vote with my enterprises” promise. Summary does not state whether an opponent can vote for another player’s support; own voting restriction covers their own vote.
answers.evidence: Parliament Meets → Voting.

answers.answer: Pay upkeep separately for every prize member even on final turn. If unpaid, return member and lose prize’s printed VP. Final turn skips Refresh and proceeds to Final Scoring. Otherwise writers return to associated Presidency Writers box; filled tokens/dividers and extra ships return supply; exhausted officers/regiments reactivate; active alliances exhaust and do not reactivate; fitted player ships keep fatigue. Advance turn and begin London Season.
answers.evidence: Upkeep and Refresh section.

answers.answer: Each shareholder may make one additional London Season retirement from supply (not Pensioners), regardless of number of firms owned, limited to highest total dividend marker among firms where they own shares. No retirement from a firm whose marker absent or zero. Spouse discounts may permit higher-cost prize; otherwise normal retirement and prestige eligibility. At start Final Scoring, score firms then allow one special retirement regardless of Company success/failure, before normal steps, with no display cards.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → Special retirement.

answers.answer: Investment and £5 per contribution go from bank to firm’s London treasury; trade revenue and dividends use India treasury. London pays ship acquisition, trade bids and expenses; firms’ expenses can use either treasury. Dividend comes only from India, and remaining India money sweeps to London. Family cash cannot be transferred into or out of firm treasuries.
answers.evidence: Deregulation intro on firm treasuries; investments; ship acquisition; expenses/dividends.

answers.answer: Firms phase occurs after Family share creation and before Hiring; investments happen without set order until no one wants more, then strategies chosen. Manager resolves timing conflicts within a firm; PM resolves conflicts between firms. Within Presidency trade, matching firm strategy reveals before any actions; trade ordering determined by initiative, with President choosing ties, or Chairman if President vacant/never successful.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → Firms phase; strategies and competing trade.

answers.answer: Firm may fit a ship from shipyard for £3 London-to-bank with shipyard owner consent. May buy player-owned Company ship with owner consent: unfatigued £3, fatigued £2, paid into Shipping treasury. Cannot acquire Company or extra ships. The summary does not specifically state “another player’s ship without consent”; consent is required to fit from a shipyard and to buy player-owned ship.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → Firms phase → Ships.

answers.answer: Hostile takeover only by player managing no firm, with consent of holders of majority target shares. Move target firm’s ships, money and shares to initiator’s charter, copy both cube positions; previous manager returns cubes and flips board to family side.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → Firms phase: Hostile takeover.

answers.answer: Merger requires managers to negotiate with every shareholder’s consent. Highest-value firm is primary; tied highest: players choose. Transfer secondary shares, ships and treasury funds to primary; secondary boards flip back to family sides. Any transfers and shares exceeding ten must be negotiated with those owners’ consent. One binding immediate agreement; primary value/dividend track remains.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → Firms phase: Merger.

answers.answer: Hobnob means no bid, trade or dividends; still pays expenses and retains its prior dividend marker for retirement. Hobnob firm ships are exempt from storms. Summary does not say other Hobnob permissions/forbidden actions beyond these.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → Firm strategies table; Firm expenses/dividends storm sentence.

answers.answer: Yes, emergency investment can occur even at ten-share cap. Use normal Company-share/workshop contribution rules; each investment pays £5 from bank to London, creates no further share above cap, pays expenses, loses any remaining cash and lowers Value one space per emergency investment. Same-turn-created Company shares remain ineligible even if traded away; summary doesn’t explicitly reaffirm otherwise for this rescue case.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → Firm expenses, rescue and dividends; investment rules.

answers.answer: Emergency negotiated merger can involve only one other firm; normal merger procedure applies, including every involved shareholder’s consent. The other firm must pay its own expenses first if unpaid, then cover endangered firm’s unpaid expenses.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → Firm expenses, rescue and dividends.

answers.answer: Voluntary dissolution requires all shareholders’ consent. Apply insolvent dissolution: shares to Debtor’s Prison at −1 VP each, ships to matching shipyards, charter flips to family side. Invested workshops remain invested for rest of game.
answers.evidence: Deregulation → Firms phase: Voluntary dissolution.

answers.answer: Each player totals VP from all firm shares they own across firms, then rounds their own fractional total down; deduct 1 VP per own family piece in Debtor’s Prison. This applies before Company outcome branch whether Company survives or fails. Company shares then gain current Court value if survives or lose it if failed; failure adds 1 VP per uninvested workshop. Firm Value per share: 1 −1; 2 0; 3–4 ½; 5–7 1; 8–9 1½; 10 2. Summary does not explain the exact Debtor’s Prison law-side effect beyond this scoring.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: firm scoring, Debtor’s Prison, branches and Value chart.
Setup → Prizes table.

answers.answer: 1710 runs turns 1–5, no deregulation procedures. 1758 runs turns 3–7 and can vote deregulation. 1813 runs 5–8 and starts deregulated. Long 1710 runs 1–8 and deregulation available separately.
answers.evidence: Setup scenario table and scenario scope rows.

answers.answer: 1710: initial Standing £10 expectations, Debt 0, each office £3, Royal Protection, one regiment per Army, no Company ships. 1758: Standing £12 expectations, Debt 3, each office £4, Calico Acts, one regiment per Army, one Company ship East Indian; Bengal control token in Bengal Presidency.
answers.evidence: Setup → Scenario figures table.

answers.answer: 1813 starts turns 5–8 with Standing £10 expectations, Debt 0, each office £3, laws Military Oversight, Deregulation (Debtor’s Prison side), Calico Acts; two regiments per Army and one Company ship per zone. Put +2/−2 share-value token in Court, create China, place Bombay/Madras/Bengal control tokens in Presidencies, return Governor General law to box and place its overlay over Director of Trade. Use Governor General instead of Director and no Governors.
answers.evidence: Setup → Scenario figures and 1813-specific setup paragraph.

answers.answer: Final turn 1–3: awards 3/1; 4–6: 5/2; 7–8: 8/4. Tied-first group each receives only lower award; no other award is distributed. The source summary does not provide a separate tie table by turn group; this rule applies to each.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Power award.

answers.answer: Initial Power positions: Social 2; Company shares 1; Shipping and Manufacturing 0. Standing expectations run £4/6/8/10/12/14/16; S reset is above £10. Deregulation lined combinations: Standing £4/6/8 and Debt 5/6/7/8; starred Standing £4 and Debt 8.
answers.evidence: Setup → Starting Power positions and Deregulation spaces.

answers.answer: No. Designer ruling says Foreign Invasion primary attack strength is ordinary die only; unrest does not add to attack or determine resulting towers. On success close all target orders once, Cascade if already all closed; Region Loss does not close them again. Event still uses Company-defense procedure and secondary unrest attacks.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings → Foreign Invasion and unrest.

answers.answer: Mercantile/Diplomatic Connection reducing a check to zero dice means failure. Company Fraud occurs at start of Revenue: roll one die per officeholder, reduce Balance by twice highest roll (minimum zero), and take bank cash equal to actual Balance reduction, so cannot overdraw. Public Demands Impeachment returns member to supply and office card to vacancies. Military Oversight demoted Commander is eligible as an officer for reappointment.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings → Applicable official errata.

answers.answer: Shared setup: Balance £5; family VP markers zero; place local alliances in named Army boxes and loot tokens money-side up in matching regions. Choose scenario card for Standing, Debt, treasuries, laws, regiments, ships and map; copy exact India towers/flags/closed orders/Elephant from card. Put Turn marker on its date and PM dial arm to matching date.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–2 and 1813/map setup paragraph.

answers.answer: Normal order: London Season → Family → Firms if deregulated → Hiring → Company Operation → Bonuses → Revenue → Events in India → Parliament Meets → Upkeep and Refresh. Eligible special Deregulation votes occur at turn start before London Season. Skip London Season on first turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure opening.

answers.answer: Retirement starts with Chairman, or former Chairman if office vacant, then clockwise. Each may retire each pensioner to a prize; it is optional. Pay printed cost; member moves to prize and gain printed VP. Set actual spending aside until London Season ends to establish selection order, then pay bank. Pensioners unused return to supplies and do not stay for another turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → London Season: Retirements.

answers.answer: No. When an empire loses its last dominated region, remove surviving capital’s starred flag; it ceases being an empire. This applies regardless of cause, including Rebellion or Company conquest.
answers.evidence: Components → India terminology: explicit last-dominated-region rule.

answers.answer: Firm share VP by Value: 1 = −1; 2 = 0; 3 = ½; 4 = ½; 5 = 1; 6 = 1; 7 = 1; 8 = 1½; 9 = 1½; 10 = 2. Each player sums all firm-share VP across firms before rounding their own fractional total down.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: firm-track VP per share and player-level rounding.
